eventMetadata.context_description: Recent numerical weather prediction models from the Korea Meteorological Administration and international ensembles indicate Seoul will experience typical late-spring conditions on May 25, with daytime maxima shaped by a building ridge of high pressure, moderate solar insolation, and light southerly flow. Ensemble guidance clusters around 26–28°C as the most probable daily high, reflecting limited moisture and weak frontal activity that curbs both strong warming and cooling. Minor model spread arises from uncertainties in boundary-layer mixing and afternoon cloud cover, keeping probabilities distributed across adjacent thresholds while assigning lower odds to extremes below 25°C or above 29°C. Updated short-range runs expected in the next 24–48 hours will refine these projections ahead of market resolution based on official observations.

eventMetadata.context_description: PAGASA’s latest outlook for Metro Manila on May 25 projects a daytime high near 35 °C with 20–30 % rain chance, consistent with the peak of the hot-dry season when solar insolation is strongest and urban heat-island effects amplify surface temperatures. Recent station readings have reached 36 °C under similar clear-to-partly-cloudy conditions, while afternoon convection or increased cloud cover can suppress the peak by 1–2 °C. Ensemble guidance shows modest spread around 34–37 °C, with the narrow 36–37 °C market spread reflecting uncertainty over exact timing of any showers and boundary-layer mixing rather than large-scale pattern shifts. Updated model runs and the official 5 a.m. bulletin on the 24th will narrow the range before resolution.
